title: Resilient downstream strategies: connection pooling, circuit breakers, and load-shedding playbook
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Problem: During the Feb 2026 regional quota surge we observed cascading failures when Redis and Kafka transient errors coincided with a spike in request fanout. Connection pools exhausted, client retries amplified downstream load, and the serving runtime violated SLOs for 95th and 99th latency. This ticket defines a set of pragmatic, deployable strategies to make downstream dependencies (Redis, Kafka, SQL) resilient: smarter connection pooling, circuit breaker policies, adaptive load-shedding, and graceful feature degradation.

Goals:
- Prevent thread/worker starvation from exhausted pools.
- Ensure deterministic degradation (documented behaviors clients can expect).
- Keep 99th percentile latency within SLO during degraded conditions by shedding excess work.
- Provide operational visibility (metrics, dashboards, runbooks) and blunt instruments for on-call.

Scope: server-side runtime and client libraries used by hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments; changes include runtime defaults, SDK changes, and console playbook UI (runbook links + kill-switch toggles). Not in scope: data model changes or user-facing UX copy beyond error codes/messages.
acceptance_criteria: New default connection pool behavior is implemented: soft limit = core * 2, hard limit = core * 10, with exponential backoff for new borrow attempts
Circuit breakers for Redis/Kafka/DB trip on error rate > 5% over 30s or latency p99 > 3s; automatic half-open probe behavior implemented
Adaptive token-bucket load-shedding at ingress that enforces SLO-consistent token consumption under overload with configurable per-route budgets
Feature-level graceful degradation implemented: non-blocking best-effort responses (cached embeddings / stale reads / reduced top-k) and clear error codes for clients
Metrics, dashboards, and alerts added: downstream_error_rate, pool_starved_count, shed_rate, circuit_state (open/closed/half-open), and on-call runbook linked
Runbook validated in chaos run (Redis latency injection) and rollback path documented; performance regressions < 5% on p50 and p90 for normal traffic
work_log: 2026-03-10 Maya Singh: Created ticket after postmortem for regional surge incident (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/postmortems/2026-02-regional-quota-surge). Initial scope drafted.

2026-03-11 Luca Ortega: Spike completed exploring connection pool libraries (HikariCP tuning + custom async pool). Decided to build on existing async pool in runtime to avoid broad SDK churn. Notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/rd/connpool-spike-ENG-16324

2026-03-12 Design review (Ava Park): Reviewed degraded response UX and error codes. Agreed on error namespace 'RWD_DOWNSTREAM_DEGRADED' and including 'retry-after' when shedding. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/designs/downstream-degradation

2026-03-13 Engineering proposal approved by TL and PM: circuit breaker thresholds, token-bucket parameters, and pool sizing heuristics. PR for initial circuit-breaker lib: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4823

2026-03-14 Luca Ortega: Implemented server-side circuit breaker + prometheus metrics. Unit tests added. Deployed to staging with Redis latency injection; observed stable shed_rate and no pool starvation. Staging dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/eng/16324-staging
2026-03-14 Ops note (Samir Patel): Added temporary kill-switch flag 'downstream_force_open' for emergency on-call use; will gate behind enterprise auth and audit logging
risks_and_tradeoffs: More aggressive shedding reduces feature availability for some customers; trade is explicit to keep SLOs and reduce latent customer impact
Tighter pool limits lower memory/connection use but increase early-request failures under extreme traffic bursts; mitigated by token-bucket smoothing and short-lived warm-up windows
Introducing circuit breakers adds complexity to client libraries for interpreting half-open probes; we standardize states via metrics and SDK helpers to reduce client burden
